subject: Subprocessor Onboard: Delegation Addendum, DPA gaps, and procurement signoff
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@cloudstream.io>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed subprocessor addition + DPA redline

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the quick call last week. We're moving forward with onboarding a third-party vendor (DataBridge Labs) that will process telemetry for their ingestion pipeline. Per our MSA flow-down obligations we attached a redline to the DPA and a short delegation addendum. The key asks from our side are:

- Confirmation that the flow-down includes audit rights (SOC2 evidence or equivalent),
- Data deletion obligations when contract terminates, and
- That any further subcontracting requires notice + written consent.

Attached: CloudStream_DPA_redline_v1.docx, Delegation_Addendum_draft.pdf

Can you confirm who from Redwood needs to sign off (legal + procurement)? We have a procurement PO hold until the delegation signoff is complete.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Legal Ops | CloudStream Solutions

---

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposed subprocessor addition + DPA redline

Forwarding CloudStream's redlines. Key items to triage below — please treat as time-sensitive, procurement is blocking the PO.

Summary notes:
- They require audit rights and data deletion language.
- Delegation addendum requires a clause that any downstream subprocessor requires written consent.
- They explicitly called out encryption/KMS ownership — they want KMS separation for EU data.

Monica — can you run the redline and map the risk to our standard DPA annex?
Karthik — procurement wants an order-form mapping and PO release conditions; can you advise on timeline?
Sean — if legal wants to propose counter-language on the consent trigger for downstream subs, please jump in.

Thanks,
Naomi
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference

---

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed subprocessor addition + DPA redline

Thanks Naomi — I reviewed the attachments and flagged the following recommended positions:

1) Audit rights: accept on SOC2 or equivalent; for audit delivery we will accept hosted report plus on-site audit with 30 days' notice (reasonable for a subprocessor).
2) Data deletion: propose standard 90-day deletion upon termination with certified destruction report.
3) Downstream consent: counter to written consent requirement — propose 'notice + objection window (10 business days)' unless the DPIA/regulatory requirement demands affirmative consent. This keeps operational flexibility for platform upgrades.
4) KMS / data residency: if they want KMS separation for EU scoped records, we need to map DataBridge's infra. If they require customer-managed keys, that's a larger product change and should be escalated.

I also tracked two redlines that materially expand liability (indemnity language) — suggest we push back. I can prepare a marked-up DPA with tracked changes and a short cover memo.

Attaching: Delegation_Addendum_review_notes.txt (summary) — will post final redline by EOD tomorrow.

Monica Patel
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed subprocessor addition + DPA redline

Looping in procurement (procurement@acme.com — placeholder for their PO team) — please note the PO release is conditional on legal signoff + a completed delegation addendum.

Timeline:
- I can get an internal PO approved within 3 business days after legal approves the DPA/addendum.
- If CloudStream requires a specific order-form signature mapping, we need their final order-form PDF (with pricing/term mapping) before I can attach the PO.

Questions for CloudStream:
1) Is the subprocessor limited to EU telemetry only or global?
2) Do they require a separate SLA/uptime commitment for the ingestion pipeline? That would affect our procurement classification.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference

Lena — thanks for the materials and patience. Next steps from Redwood:

- Monica will produce a redline with proposed alternative language for downstream consent and indemnity (expected EOD 11 Aug).
- I asked Karthik to confirm PO timing once legal signs off; procurement expects final order form PDF.
- Sean will weigh in on any high-risk indemnity exposure and escalate if needed.

Quick clarifying Qs:
- Can you confirm whether DataBridge will handle both EU and US telemetry? That determines whether we need KMS separation.
- Do you have a contact at DataBridge we can add to the thread for technical mapping?

If we can get answers today we can aim to finalize items for procurement by Wednesday EOD.

Best,
Naomi

From: Lena Ortiz <lena@cloudstream.io>

Hi all — quick answers:

- DataBridge will process telemetry globally (EU + US).
- DataBridge contact: Marco Ruiz <marco@databridgelabs.com> (cc'd on their side in a separate email thread this afternoon).
- They do not currently support customer-managed KMS keys but can provide encryption-at-rest with our tenant keys; they indicated they can explore KMS separation as an implementation project (timeline 6-8 weeks).

I uploaded the supporting SOC2 summary and a short vendor security questionnaire to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cCS-CloudStream-DPA

We'll await Monica's redline. We prefer a signed addendum + DPA confirmation to avoid delaying our PO.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
